CH-SRM-01 | Version 1.0 | Effective 01 Sep 2026
About Cedarhaven. The Town of Cedarhaven is a fictional Ontario municipality created for a technical
recruitment exercise. This operational guide describes its simulated municipal 311 service-request
process. It is not a real government policy, contact directory or statement of Canadian law.
Core service promise. Residents can report non-emergency municipal service issues through one
front door, receive a tracking number, and check progress. Submitting a request does not guarantee
that the Town will approve a permit, issue a by-law penalty, or complete work by a particular date.
Use this guide for
• Missed curbside waste collection and damaged municipal bins.
• Potholes, damaged street signs, municipal streetlights and blocked catch basins.
• Park maintenance, fallen public trees and unsafe municipal pathways.
• Request intake, classification, response targets, status tracking and escalation.

SRM 1 | How to submit a service request
Contact routes, intake fields and what happens next
1.1 Accepted channels
Channel
Availability / what to expect
Cedarhaven Service Portal
Available for electronic submissions at any time; automated reference
number after successful submission.
311 contact centre
Staffed Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., excluding Town-observed
holidays.
Town Hall front desk
Staff can help record requests during the same business hours; no separate
priority.
Accessible intake
Residents may request telephone assistance or alternate-format
confirmation via 311 during staffed hours.
The guide deliberately does not provide a public website URL, street address, email address or
telephone number other than the generic 311 service name. Do not invent one.
1.2 Intake information
• Required: issue category, location or nearest intersection, clear description, and date first noticed
(if known).
• Useful but optional: photo, hazard description, reference landmark, and a contact method for
updates.
• For a missed collection, the collection date, material type, set-out time and bin condition are
additionally needed (see page 4).
• Requests involving private property may require landowner consent before municipal staff can
enter.
1.3 Eligibility and ownership
The 311 team checks whether the issue concerns a Town-owned asset or Town-managed service. It
may forward eligible by-law complaints to Enforcement and permit questions to Development
Services. Routing is not a promise that an investigation or approval will occur.
Safety first. For immediate danger to life, fire, suspected gas leaks or a serious active medical
emergency, contact emergency services. Do not treat a 311 submission as an emergency response.
For an immediate water-main break, contact 311 during staffed hours; outside those hours the guide
does not provide an after-hours phone number.

2.2 How time is measured
• Business day: Monday-Friday excluding Town-observed holidays.
• Staffed hour: time within the 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. weekday contact-centre schedule.
• An online request filed outside staffed hours enters the triage queue at the next staffed opening.

Acknowledgement confirms receipt and issues a case identifier. Assessment identifies severity,
jurisdiction and next action. Make-safe addresses an immediate hazard. Resolution records the final
outcome. These are not interchangeable.
Important exception. A fallen overhead utility wire is treated as an immediate hazard; residents
must keep clear and contact emergency services or the utility provider. A 311 case can be recorded
for coordination, but it must not delay the emergency notification.

SRM 3 | Curbside waste and missed collection
Eligibility criteria, evidence, collection attempt and exceptions
3.1 When to report a missed pickup
A missed garbage, recycling or organics pickup may be reported after 7:00 p.m. on the scheduled
collection day and within two business days after that day. Early reports are recorded as inquiries,
not confirmed missed-collection service requests.
3.2 What residents must provide
• Full service address, material stream (garbage, recycling or organics), scheduled collection date
and time the bin was set out.
• Whether the bin was visible and accessible at the curb by 7:00 a.m. on collection day.
• Whether a rejection tag was attached, the lid was closed, and any vehicle or snowbank blocked
access.
• A photo is helpful but not mandatory; personal contact information is optional unless an update is
requested.
3.3 Eligibility and attempt window
Situation
Town response
On-time, compliant set-out; no obstruction
Accept missed-collection case and target a return pickup
within 2 business days after validation.
Bin placed out after 7:00 a.m.
Not eligible for a missed-pickup return; advise next scheduled
day.
Rejection tag for contamination / oversized
contents
Not eligible until corrected; advise resident to follow collection
rules.
Blocked by parked vehicle, snowbank or
inaccessible gate
May be declined; resident should remove the obstruction
before next service.
After a valid report, residents should leave the bin at the curb until 7:00 p.m. of the next business
day, unless doing so creates a safety obstruction. A return pickup is a target, not a guarantee.

holiday collection schedules, missed-collection fines or the full list of acceptable recyclable
materials. The assistant should not infer those details.

SRM 4 | Roads, streetlights, drainage and water
Category-specific routing and field service standards
4.1 Potholes and roadway surfaces
For routine potholes on Town-maintained roads (P3), Roads Operations targets an assessment within
3 business days and a repair within 15 business days after assessment, subject to weather and
materials. Report the nearest address or intersection, travel direction, lane and hazard size if safe.
A road collapse, sinkhole or hazard causing immediate danger is P1; see page 3. Provincial highways,
private roads and roads outside Cedarhaven are referred to their owners and are not scheduled as
Town repairs.
4.2 Streetlights and traffic signs
Issue
Target or rule
Flickering or unlit Town streetlight
P3 assessment within 3 business days; repair target 10 business
days after assessment if Town-owned.
Damaged stop sign
P2 initial assessment within 1 business day; make-safe / temporary
control according to field risk.
Traffic-signal outage
Urgent safety referral to Roads Operations; if traffic is dangerous
contact emergency services.
Private driveway or private parking-lot
light
Outside the Town streetlight program; contact property owner.
4.3 Flooding and blocked catch basins
A blocked catch basin with standing water but no immediate roadway danger is normally P2 if a road
is affected, otherwise P3. Flooding entering occupied buildings or undermining a roadway requires
urgent safety escalation; do not promise a drainage response time beyond the priority assessment
target.
4.4 Suspected water-main break
Provide the location, visible leak description and any hazard. 311 records a referral to Water
Operations. Water shutoff time, repair completion time and compensation eligibility are not defined
in this guide. Residents should avoid affected areas and follow any official safety direction.

Service ownership, environmental factors and boundaries
5.1 Parks and pathways
Issue
Guidance
Overflowing garbage bin in a Town park
P3 assessment within 3 business days; cleaning target
within 5 business days after assessment.
Broken play-equipment component
Classify P1 if imminent injury risk; otherwise P2; field team
decides whether to close the feature.
Unsafe debris or glass on busy public pathway
P1 if acute injury risk, otherwise P2 or P3 after assessment.
Graffiti on Town-owned park structure
P3 assessment; cleaning target within 10 business days
after assessment.
5.2 Public and private trees
For a tree or large branch blocking a public sidewalk, record location, obstruction and visible hazard;
usually P2. For a downed tree resting on a power line, keep clear and seek emergency/utility
assistance. Routine public-tree pruning is P3, with field scheduling dependent on season and arborist
availability.
A tree entirely on private property is generally the owner's responsibility. If it violates a
property-maintenance standard or creates an apparent nuisance, the resident may submit a by-law
complaint under CH-BYL-02; municipal crews do not automatically cut private trees.
5.3 Sidewalk and winter-maintenance reports
• Broken municipal sidewalk slab: routine P3 unless an acute trip hazard raises the priority.
• Snow or ice on a Town sidewalk: assess according to weather event and pedestrian safety;
normal time-to-clear is not published here.
• Snow or ice on a private frontage: may be a by-law matter under CH-BYL-02; the Town does not
guarantee private-property clearing via 311.
Limits. No routine street-sweeping dates, park opening hours, tree-pruning calendar, snowplow map
or road-closure schedule are specified in these recruitment documents.

SRM 6 | Request lifecycle and resident updates
A trackable case is not the same as an approved action
6.1 Standard status definitions
Status
Meaning / action
Submitted
Request received and assigned a reference number; completeness not yet
checked.
Under Review
Staff checks scope, location, evidence, duplication and priority.
Assigned
Responsible Town work group or partner has accepted the item for assessment
or action.
Scheduled
Work visit or next action planned; no fixed appointment implied.
In Progress
Field or desk team has started the task or investigation.
Completed
Town has recorded its action or final decision; may include referral or
no-work-required outcome.
Closed - Not Eligible
Outside jurisdiction, duplicate, insufficient information or ineligible service.
6.2 How updates work
• The Service Portal shows the current status and most recent status note for users with a valid
case reference.
• If the resident supplied an email and opted into updates, a notification is sent when the case is
Assigned, Scheduled or Completed.
• If the resident did not provide contact details, the case can still be processed, but proactive
personal notifications are unavailable.
• Sensitive enforcement information may be withheld from the resident-facing case notes.
6.3 Reopening
A resident may request review of a completed service request within five business days after its
completion if the reported condition persists. Reopening is discretionary after staff verification; after
five business days, a new case should generally be filed. By-law investigations have separate
disclosure and appeal procedures (CH-BYL-02).
Dates matter. A Scheduled status is not a guaranteed visit date. The published performance targets
concern categories and initial actions; never invent an individual crew appointment or a specific
arrival time.

SERVICE REQUEST MANAGEMENT
SRM 7 | Duplicates, escalation and cross-service routing
Protect resident privacy and avoid the wrong workflow
7.1 Duplicate prevention
Requests may be considered duplicates if they concern the same location, issue category and
observed condition within 72 hours, subject to staff review. A resident may be linked to the existing
case rather than given an independent repair schedule. Materially worsening hazards are re-triaged
even when an earlier case exists.
7.2 Escalation rules
• If a P3 request has not been assessed after 3 business days, residents may ask 311 for a status
review.
• If a category-specific completion target has passed, 311 may send a follow-up to the owning work
group; this does not guarantee immediate completion.
• If a hazard becomes urgent, residents should report the changed conditions instead of relying on
the previous priority.
• For a submitted permit or business-licence application, contact Development Services through
the process described in CH-PER-03.
7.3 Which process owns the issue?
Resident situation
Correct route
Noise from a nearby renovation
By-law complaint (CH-BYL-02), unless immediate danger.
Need approval to build a new deck
Permit application (CH-PER-03), not a service request.
Contractor blocks the public sidewalk with
materials
311 obstruction report; Development Services may also
review encroachment permit compliance.
Construction appears to violate approved permit
Development Services compliance review; 311 can route
the concern.
Missed waste pickup
311 waste service request if eligible under page 4.
7.4 Privacy and records
Only collect information reasonably needed to process the case. Do not publish resident phone
numbers, exact contact details or enforcement witness statements in public answer text. Internal
case notes and third-party identities are not available through this public guide.

1.1 Residential amplified sound
Amplified music, outdoor speakers and similar amplified sound must not create unreasonable
disturbance in residential areas during 10:00 p.m.-7:00 a.m. on all days. During other hours,
persistent excessive noise may still be reviewed if the facts support a nuisance concern; the hours
are not a blanket permission to disturb neighbours.

follows this schedule. The rule applies to private contractors as well as homeowners. A building
permit does not extend permissible noise hours.
1.3 Narrow exemptions
• Immediate emergency repair: work needed to prevent imminent danger or restore an essential
utility may occur outside the routine construction window.
• Town-authorized emergency operations: municipal emergency crews may operate when needed

building permit is not such an exemption.

A homeowner using a power saw at 8:00 a.m. Saturday is outside the permitted window. The same
activity at 10:00 a.m. Saturday is within the routine construction-noise window, although other
by-law standards may still apply. An emergency utility repair at 2:00 a.m. can qualify only if the facts
meet the emergency exception.

BYL 2 | Property standards and outdoor maintenance
Grass, waste accumulation, vacant properties and notices
2.1 Grass and vegetation
From May 1 to September 30, maintained portions of residential front and side yards must not have
unmanaged grass or weeds exceeding 20 cm in height. Deliberately maintained naturalized gardens
are not automatically a violation; Enforcement evaluates maintenance, sightlines and nuisance
conditions.
2.2 Outdoor accumulation
• Garbage, loose food waste or household debris must not accumulate outdoors in a way that
attracts pests or creates a health nuisance.
• Construction materials may be stored temporarily on the private worksite if reasonably organized
and safe; material on a public sidewalk requires separate encroachment approval (CH-PER-03).
• A resident should not enter a neighbour's yard to photograph a suspected violation. Photos taken
legally from public areas may be submitted.
2.3 Typical enforcement sequence
Step
Standard practice
Observe / verify
Officer assesses the location and available evidence before finding a
breach.
Written compliance notice
For ordinary vegetation or storage violations, the notice generally gives 7
calendar days to correct.
Reinspection
Officer checks after the stated period; more action may follow if the breach
remains.
Immediate hazard exception
If there is an urgent public safety hazard, the Town may act or refer
urgently without waiting 7 days.
2.4 Complaints involving vacant lots
Vacant private lots are subject to the outdoor storage and hazard provisions. Ownership verification
and access restrictions can delay investigation. The Town cannot promise a clean-up date simply
because a complaint has been filed.
Scope distinction. Overflowing public park bins and debris on Town-owned paths are municipal
maintenance issues under CH-SRM-01, not private-property enforcement cases.

5.1 Persistent barking
Persistent dog barking may be investigated when reported with approximate dates, duration,
location and description of the disturbance. This fictional by-law does not set a fixed number of barks
or minutes automatically constituting an offence. A neighbour's identity and personal details are not
publicly disclosed.
5.2 Animals at large and immediate danger
Report a loose domestic animal through 311 for referral to Animal Services. If a person faces
immediate attack or serious danger, contact emergency services. The Town does not promise animal
retrieval times in these exercise documents.
5.3 Business premises and patios
• A restaurant operating a seasonal sidewalk patio may need a business licence and a separate
public-right-of-way encroachment permit under CH-PER-03.
• Ordinary business-licence issuance does not authorize obstructing a public sidewalk.
• Outdoor amplified music remains subject to the residential noise rule where applicable; a patio
permit does not grant a noise exemption.
5.4 Community events
A large outdoor event may require a special-event review with other departments. The guide does
not establish an attendee threshold, permit fee, booking availability or special-event application
deadline. An official event approval may include site-specific conditions, but no such approval is
included here.
5.5 Enforcement boundaries
A report of a neighbour's unlicensed business can be routed for review; Enforcement does not
publicly confirm the subject's account status. Building safety issues and structural modifications are
routed to Development Services rather than decided solely under this guide.

complainant identities or past confidential enforcement file outcomes when answering resident

BYL 6 | Complaints, inspection and outcome
An allegation is not a determination of non-compliance
6.1 Filing and basic evidence
Submit a non-emergency complaint through 311 or the Cedarhaven Service Portal as described in
CH-SRM-01. Include the location, type of concern, approximate dates/times, what was observed and
any legally obtained supporting photos. Anonymous complaints may be accepted but can be harder
to verify.
6.2 Intake and investigation workflow
Stage
Meaning
Submitted
Complaint logged; complainant receives a case reference if available.
Triage
Enforcement checks jurisdiction, urgency, duplicates and sufficiency of details.
Investigation
Officer may review records, inspect from lawful vantage points, or seek further
evidence.
Notice / education
If verified, officer may issue guidance or a written compliance notice.
Reinspection / action
Officer verifies correction and decides whether a further enforcement measure
is appropriate.
Closed
Case concluded, including no violation found, lack of evidence or successful
compliance.
6.3 Timelines and limits
• Non-urgent complaints target triage within 3 business days. This is not a promise of inspection or
resolution within three days.
• Urgent public safety concerns are referred for immediate risk-based response; contact
emergency services when life safety is at issue.
• For common property-standard notices, the typical correction window is 7 calendar days after
service (see page 3).
• Investigation duration depends on evidence, property access, repeat visits and legal process. No
universal completion deadline is stated.
6.4 Disclosure to complainant
Residents may receive limited status information such as "under review" or "closed". Officer notes,
personal details of alleged offenders, witness identities and penalty records are not automatically
released through 311 or the chatbot.
No guaranteed outcome. A report does not automatically cause a citation, ticket, licence
suspension, removal of a structure or entry onto private property.

Thresholds are specific to this exercise and not real law
1.1 Small detached storage-shed exemption
A detached storage shed accessory to a single detached dwelling is exempt from a Cedarhaven
building permit only when all of these conditions are satisfied:
• Floor area is 12.0 square metres or less (exactly 12.0 m2 qualifies).
• Total structure height is 3.0 metres or less.
• No plumbing or electrical service is installed.
• It is not used for sleeping, commercial occupancy or another habitable use.
• It is entirely outside registered utility easements and does not conflict with a required setback.
If any condition fails, a building-permit review is required. Example: a 14 m2 storage shed requires a
building permit even if it is only 2.5 m high. A 10 m2 shed with electrical wiring also requires a permit
review.
1.2 Zoning and other rules still apply
The exemption is solely from the building-permit requirement. It does not exempt the shed from
setbacks, lot coverage, easements, heritage restrictions or applicable noise limits. This document
does not publish the numeric setback distances or lot-coverage percentages.

An ordinary residential fence generally does not require a building permit, but height restrictions
remain under CH-BYL-02, BYL 4. A new private outdoor swimming pool requires a separate
pool-barrier permit; ordinary-fence permit exemption does not apply to pool barriers.

unless a specific written detour arrangement is approved. A permit does not authorize dangerous
materials on the footpath or override emergency access needs.
